summary: Humberto Maturana studied at the University of Chile, University College London, and Harvard University (doctorate, 1956–1958). A philosopher who taught Francisco Varela, he held posts at MIT, the University of Chile, UIUC, and founded Instituto Matríztica in 2000.

Working in history, archaeology, and Indology, Humphrey William Codrington studied at Winchester College and New College, Oxford (B.A. 1898–1902). He served in the Ceylon Civil Service from 1903 to 1932.

Hung Wu is an art historian and sinologist who earned degrees at the Central Academy of Fine Arts and Harvard (PhD ~1980–1987). His faculty appointments include Harvard, the University of Chicago, New York University, and the University of Oxford.
Hung-Yi Yang is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. Yang earned a PhD at the University of Sydney, where Mark Allon served as doctoral supervisor (attested 2013).

Huston Smith was a scholar of religion and philosophy who studied at Central Methodist University, University of Chicago Divinity School (PhD ~1940–1945), and under Zuigan Goto. He held professorships at MIT (1958–1973), Syracuse University (1973–1983), and UC Berkeley (~1984–1999).

Huynh Kim Lan is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned a Master of Arts in Buddhist Studies at Mahachulalongkornrajavidyalaya University, advised by Phra Suthithammanuwat and Veerachart Nimanong (attested 2010).
Huynh Thi Ha Vy is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts at the International Buddhist College, studying under Kapila Abhayawansa.
Hwansoo Kim is a scholar in Buddhist and religious studies. Kim has held posts as Professor at Duke University (attested 2017) and Professor of Religious Studies at Yale University (attested 2026).

Hyacinth Bitchurin was a scholar of Sinology and Iranian and Central Asian studies. Educated at Kazan Theological Academy, he served as Rector of Tobolsk Theological Seminary, worked for the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs, and founded Kyakhta School of Chinese Language.

Hyakudai Sakamoto was a philosopher who studied at the University of Tokyo. He held posts at Aoyama Gakuin University, Tokyo University of Pharmacy and Life Sciences, and The Open University of Japan.

Hyejeong Choi is a scholar of history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies who earned a PhD at Ohio State University under John C. Huntington. Choi was an attested visiting researcher at the Archaeological Institute of Kashihara in 2015.

Hyla Stuntz Converse was a scholar of Indology and religious studies. She earned a B.D. from Union Theological Seminary (1949) and a Ph.D. from Columbia University (1971), and held a post at Oklahoma State University in 1974.

Hyon Gak Sunim is a Buddhist studies figure who studied at Yale University (~1983–1987), Harvard University (~1989–1992), and the University of Freiburg, and trained under traditional teacher Seungsahn Haengwon (~1990–2004).

Hyoung Seok Ham specializes in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy, completing a Ph.D. at the University of Michigan (2009–2016) under Madhav M. Deshpande. Ham held appointments at Kyushu University (2017–2019) and Chonnam National University (2019).
Hywel David Lewis was a philosopher and scholar of religion who studied at Bangor University and Jesus College, Oxford. He held an academic post at Bangor University from ~1936 to 1955.

Hélène Brunner-Lachaux was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied under Jean Filliozat and at EPHE (diploma 1962). She held posts at the French Institute of Pondicherry and the National Centre for Scientific Research (1963–1985).

Hürelbaatar Ujeed is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned a Ph.D. in Social Anthropology from the University of Cambridge. Ujeed serves as Professor and Principal Investigator at Inner Mongolia University for Nationalities.

Ian Harris was a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who earned his doctorate at Lancaster University (1985). He co-founded the UK Association for Buddhist Studies and held posts at St Martin's College and the University of Cumbria.

Ian James Coghlan specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a doctorate in Asian Studies from La Trobe University in 2004 and served as a research fellow at Monash University's Monash Asia Institute (attested 2005).

Ian Kesarcodi-Watson was a philosopher and Indologist who studied at Melbourne, Oxford, McMaster, and Savitribai Phule Pune University (Ph.D. 1982). He lectured in philosophy at the University of Hong Kong (1971–1975) and La Trobe University (1975–1984).
